## Product-source drift

The authoritative AgentSight repository published `v1.0.4` on `2026-08-10` from commit `ac1e6cb7a8398c57c1ad0ba04ff032cd271d99c8`. The release adds Cursor IDE sessions through the agent-native local-session path. The website still advertises `v1.0.3` and pins the product snapshot to `07a83a32257b8c8dcba911bd9db23f77e71dc085`, so this is material product drift that requires synchronization before routine SEO experimentation.

The product implementation and documentation establish the Cursor boundary precisely:

- Cursor transcripts are discovered below `~/.cursor/projects/<workspace>/agent-transcripts/`;
- delegated `subagents/*.jsonl` work is folded into the parent session and can update the session candidate freshness;
- transcripts provide prompts, assistant output, tool calls, file activity, and event timestamps;
- Cursor's local `state.vscdb` can enrich session timing, model, and working directory, while the parser degrades to transcript-only data when the database is unavailable or locked;
- no `sudo` and no special Cursor launch is required for the agent-native path;
- normal AgentSight eBPF/TLS capture is not the supported Cursor route: desktop platform support, Electron's stripped/helper-process TLS boundary, and Cursor's protobuf Connect payloads are independent obstacles;
- recent Cursor versions may not contain local per-turn token usage, so absent recent token totals are an expected source limitation rather than proof of a capture failure.

No broader compatibility or customer claim is inferred from this release.

## Semantic-overlap and research brief

- Proposed canonical: `/integrations/cursor/`
- Page type: integration reference
- Reader: an engineer using Cursor who wants AgentSight visibility into existing IDE agent sessions
- Reader decision: use AgentSight's agent-native local-session path; do not try to wrap Cursor with `record` or infer successful observability from an Electron TLS attach
- Existing-page overlap: current Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode/OpenClaw integration pages focus on CLI/runtime/process/TLS boundaries. The closed-source-CLI use case explains why external observation can help, but it does not own Cursor's local transcript/state model. The Cursor question therefore has a distinct mechanism, workflow, source set, and acceptance test.
- Durable information gain: exact `v1.0.4` implementation boundary, two-source local data model, delegated-subagent folding, agent-native versus live-capture comparison, current token/timestamp limitations, and public-safe commands.
- Primary sources: AgentSight `v1.0.4` release, exact `v1.0.4` `docs/agents.md`, AgentSight PR `#149`, Cursor's Agent tools documentation, and Cursor's subagent release material.
- Claims deliberately avoided: live Cursor API-body capture, recent token totals as a guaranteed metric, support for every Electron IDE agent, or eBPF support on macOS/Windows.
- Internal next decisions: observation-boundary use case, Agent Flamegraph guide, and Security/data handling.
